events.text: You have been awake a long time when you first understand the robes. A man fell in the pool last spring, drowned and quiet, in good purple silk. You have thought about how it hung. You could be that long, and that straight. The old stories on the bank are about something like you, walking to a house at night. You had taken them for slander.

choices.text: Try it, some night with no moon

effects.log: You come up the bank on two legs like something learning to lie. It holds for a hundred steps. It will hold for more.

choices.text: No. You have waited a long time for the sky, not for a roof

effects.log: You sink back down. It is very quiet, and it stays quiet for a good while, and you are almost sure that you meant it.

events.text: The first road is hard. Feet are absurd, and the frogs go silent as you pass. There is a house at the end of a dyke with a lamp in the back room, and someone inside mending by it and singing the wrong words to a harvest song. You stand in the dark and listen to a whole verse. The rooster in that yard has very good lungs. You had better start back.

choices.text: Learn the song, and come back

effects.log: You hum it all the way down to the bottom of the pool. The carp take no notice. You have it right by autumn, the wrong words and all.

choices.text: Take a look at the rooster on your way past

effects.log: It sees you first, and it says so. You go home very fast, on whatever you have.

events.text: At the village well, late, an old drunk asks you for a light as if it were nothing. You have no idea what a light is. He looks at your hands, at the wet hem of your robe, and at the road that goes nowhere but the pool. "Ah," he says, and he pats your arm. "My grandmother told me about you. Mind the thread." He goes in. You stand there a good while, being told.

choices.text: Find out what the thread is

effects.log: You lie under the wash-stones for a season, listening to the women. It is an old story. The girl always does it, and her father always tells her to. So now you know that much.

choices.text: Follow him, and leave a fish on his step

effects.log: He finds it in the morning, and he nods at the pool on his way to the fields. It is the first time that anyone has been polite to you.

events.text: A festival: lanterns on the river, drums, everyone slightly too loud. Nobody looks twice at one more stranger in a good robe, and that is a very strange feeling after five hundred years. A child sells you a rice cake and you do not know what to give for it. You give her a river pearl. She bites it, and she looks up, and she runs for her mother, shouting.

choices.text: Be somewhere else, quickly

effects.log: By the time they come back with a lantern, there is a wet place on the road. It will be a good story in that village, and it will get better.

choices.text: Stay, and let them look at you

effects.log: You stand there and bow, badly. They are too polite to ask. The whole village brings you things to eat, and you do not sleep for a week afterwards.

events.text: {npc} is sitting on the back step at the dead of night, mending a net by no light at all. {He} does not get up. "You are the one from the pool," {he} says. "You come every month, and stand by the persimmon, and you hum my song, badly." {He} bites off the thread. "It is a long way to come to be bad at something. Sit down, if you are sitting."

choices.text: Sit down

effects.log: You sit. It is harder than you thought it would be. {He} goes on mending, and tells you what is wrong with the second verse. You leave when the sky turns grey, and you are smiling, with a face you only half own.

choices.text: Go back to the water, and do not come again

effects.log: You go. {He} does not call after you. The persimmon drops its fruit all that autumn with nobody standing under it.

events.text: You bring {npc} the only things you own: a sword from the riverbed, three pearls, a gold cup with somebody's crest. {He} looks at them on the step for some time. "So you drowned a lot of people," {he} says. You did not drown them. They came as they were. {He} seems to think this needs saying out loud, and to take some time over it. Then {he} asks whether you eat.

choices.text: Tell {him} about the boats that went down without you

effects.log: You talk until the rooster clears its throat. You did not know that you remembered so many of them. {He} keeps the cup, and gives it to the headman, for the ferry.

choices.text: Say that you have sunk a boat or two, and that you are sorry

effects.log: {He} looks at you for a long time, and {he} nods, and takes nothing. "Come back when you have stopped," {he} says. You do not sink anything for a long while.

events.text: It is raining, because you are happy, and you have not worked out how to stop that. The whole dyke is going. {npc} comes out to the back door with a lantern and the rain in {his} face. "Is this you?" {he} asks. "The Bak family has a field down there." You have never once in your life considered the Bak family's field.

choices.text: Stop the rain. It takes some doing

effects.log: It goes on for an hour after you stop, out of habit. The field is wet and whole. Nobody thanks you, and {he} brings you out a bowl of something hot, and you take it to mean the same.

choices.text: Tell {him} it will not hurt the field. Be wrong

effects.log: It does hurt the field. {He} is out there all the next week in the mud with the Baks, and you can see {him} from the pool, not looking your way.

events.text: There is no one to marry you, and neither of you wants one. {npc} sets out two bowls on the step at the dark of the moon and pours water in both. "I know what the end of the old story is," {he} says. "I have read it on every wash-stone in this valley. I would like it known I was told." {He} holds out a bowl. It is only water, and your hand is not quite steady.

choices.text: Drink. And before dawn, go home, as you always will

effects.log: You drink. {He} drinks. Before dawn you are a very long way down, with that small plain taste still in your mouth, and the whole pool seems warmer, which it is not.

choices.text: Set it down. It has never ended well for the one who stays

effects.log: You set the bowl down on the step, and you go. In the morning {he} pours both of them on the persimmon. {He} is not a person who wastes water.

events.text: You come up before dawn with a fish, because you still cannot think of anything else to bring. {npc} has stopped pretending to be surprised. The roof leaks by the east wall. You look at that for a while, and then you lie on the roof all of one night, thinking, in your own shape, in the rain, and the rain goes around. It is the most foolish thing that you have done in a thousand years.

choices.text: Do it again next time it rains

effects.log: It never leaks again, on that one roof in the valley. The neighbours begin to talk, in a friendly way. {He} says nothing, and starts leaving the back door on the latch.

choices.text: Get down before anyone looks out

effects.log: You are nearly back in the water when the rooster goes. You have started to hate that bird with all the patience you have.

events.text: {npc} has started asking questions, sideways, while {he} works. What is it like at the bottom? Is it dark? Are you cold? You have never had to put any of it into words, and they come out wrong, one by one, on the step before dawn. "So you are lonely," {he} says, and {he} bites the thread. You did not say that. You go through all of it again, and you did.

choices.text: Ask what it is like up here

effects.log: So {he} tells you about being tired, and owing the headman for seed, and having a bad knee in the wet. It is much the most interesting thing that you have heard in centuries.

choices.text: Say that it is not cold, and leave it

effects.log: You leave it. {He} lets you. On your next visit there is a quilted jacket on the step, far too small for anything that you are, and you take it down with you anyway.

events.text: Somebody has told the headman, {npc}. {He} comes up to the pool alone with a jar of the good wine and pours it in, and stands with {his} hat in {his} hands, and says to the water, carefully, that the family on the dyke are decent people, and pay on time, and that {he} would take it very kindly if they were to come to no harm. {He} waits a while. {He} has a lot of courage for a small person.

choices.text: Let a very large ripple go across the pool, gently

effects.log: {He} goes down the hill rather quickly and tells nobody what {he} saw. The offerings at that pool are better from then on, and they are left with a bit more manners.

choices.text: Lie still. {He} should not be sure

effects.log: {He} stands there till dark, and goes home not knowing. Good. That will do {him} no harm. But you find that you have counted {his} steps all the way down to the dyke.

events.text: You feel it halfway down the bank: a small cold tug at the hem. There is a thread in the robe, run in with a needle, just where you would not see it. It goes back up the road in the dark. You know this story, and so does everyone. In the morning it will lead someone to the water. It is {npc}'s own red thread. {He} was singing when you left, and {he} did not look round.

choices.text: Break it, and say nothing

effects.log: It snaps like a hair. You go up in a month as if nothing had happened, and {he} looks at the hem, and at you, and pours you some water. It will never be spoken of.

choices.text: Let it run. Lie in the shallows, and wait for the morning

effects.log: {He} comes down at first light, alone, winding it round {his} hand. {He} stops at the edge. "Well," {he} says, after a long while. "Your second verse is still wrong." So there is nothing left to tell.

choices.text: Cut it off with the hem, and do not go back

effects.log: You leave the red end lying on the road, for {him} to find. That is the kindest thing you know how to do. It is not very kind.

events.text: {npc}'s father has come back from the salt road and heard. The father does not rage. The father sits at the table and runs a needle through red thread, slowly, in front of {him}, and sets it down between them. "Your grandmother's sister did this," says the father. "That sister had the child. Nobody ever saw the child without a hat." The father looks out at the dark, right at the persimmon, and at you.

choices.text: Walk in at the front door, in the robe, and sit down

effects.log: It is the longest meal of your life. Nobody eats. The father looks at your hands, and pours you a cup, and the hand is quite steady. You like the father very much. The father will never forgive you.

choices.text: Let the river come up a hand's width in the night, for the father to see

effects.log: It takes the bottom step and no more. Nobody says anything about needles again, and they do not say very much to you either.

choices.text: Stay away for a year, until the father goes

effects.log: The father goes in the spring. {npc} does not ask where you were. There is a good deal {he} has stopped asking.

events.text: There is a child. {npc} tells you with {his} back turned, on the step, the winter before. Now there it is in the crook of {his} arm, called {bk_child}, red in the face and very loud, with one foot rather cold. You have held a sword and a boat and a good many drowned men. You are given this and you hold it as you have never held anything. It looks at you, and it stops crying.

choices.text: Look for the scales

effects.log: None. You go over every finger. Ten, and pink, and warm, with a bad temper. You put it back very gently, and you do not know what it is that you feel, and it may be relief.

choices.text: Hum it the second verse

effects.log: Badly. It goes to sleep, either way. {npc} tells you that you have finally got it right, and you know that {he} is lying.

events.text: A second one, called {bk_child}, and you are told about it this time in good order, and you come up specially, and you bring a fish. {npc} is very tired and laughs at the fish. You are not sure how many there have been of your kind who have stood in a back room in a borrowed robe holding one of these, at this hour, with that bird out there in the dark clearing its throat.

choices.text: Stay past the rooster, just this once

effects.log: It crows. You are still there. Your feet are not doing very well, and the left hand is starting to go, and nobody says anything about it. You see the sun come in on them.

choices.text: Hand it back and go, as you always will

effects.log: You are in the deep by first light. You lie very still all of that day. You had not known you could be homesick for a place that you could see.

events.text: {bk_child} is seven this year, and you watched the whole of one summer from the reeds for a sign. {bk_child} can't hold a breath in the shallows. The cold water makes for a cough. {bk_child} throws stones at the heron, misses, and goes home to dinner. A perfectly ordinary child. {bk_love} sees you in the reeds and, for once, does not look away, and shakes {bk_love}'s own head a very little.

choices.text: Be glad

effects.log: You are. You find that you really are, mostly. An ordinary life is a long way to fall from nothing, and nobody will ever come to that house with a needle or a hook.

choices.text: Watch for one more summer, in case

effects.log: There is nothing. You see a child with skinned knees, learning to swear. It is a good summer, as they go, and you are not proud of why you stayed.

events.text: {bk_child} is seven, and has gone into the pool again, and it has been much too long. {bk_love} is on the bank, not screaming, which is worse. You come up under the small thing in the dark and it opens its eyes down there, at the depth where nothing human opens them, and looks at you, and is not at all afraid. It pats your snout. It has not taken a breath in some time and sees no reason to.

choices.text: Carry it up. Then tell {bk_love} what you both know

effects.log: You lie in the shallows while the child coughs and laughs. {bk_love} wraps it in a jacket, and looks at it, and at you. "Hat," says {bk_love} at last. "It will need a hat." So the blood goes on. It will go on after you, and it knows the way down.

choices.text: Carry it up, and tell it never to come down here again

effects.log: You say it in your own voice. It looks at you and nods, as a child nods. It will be back. You knew that already, and so does the water, and it will go on knowing in someone not yet born.

events.text: {npc}'s hair is white. You had noticed, you think, as you notice the seasons. {He} takes the step one at a time now, and {he} has a stick, and when you come up before dawn {he} has been up already for a while, because {he} does not sleep. You are exactly as you were. {He} takes your wet hand and turns it over. "You have not changed a scale," {he} says, "and I have been meaning to complain about that."

choices.text: Come every night now, and let the rooster say what it likes

effects.log: You lose some skin that way, and most of your dignity. {He} tells you the whole valley's business, over and over. You have never in a thousand years been so well informed.

choices.text: Ask what {he} wants from you, while you can still do it

effects.log: {He} thinks it over for some time. "The second verse," {he} says. "Get it right, before I go." So that is what you do with your thousand years, that winter, on a back step.

events.text: It is a wet morning at the end of the dyke, and the back door is on the latch. They carry {bk_love} up the hill in the rain, and the whole valley walks behind, and most of them glance once at the pool as they pass. There is a bowl of water standing on the step. You did not know that you could not cry. You make it rain for nine days, and for once nobody says anything about the field.

choices.text: Let it rain

effects.log: On the tenth day it stops. The persimmon is in leaf, and someone has started to hum in the back room, the wrong words, a child of a child. You lie still and listen to all of it.

choices.text: Go up the hill by night, and lie down beside the mound, for a year

effects.log: They find the track of you in the grass in spring, as wide as a road, and they do not mow there. It is a small hill. There is a small pool at the foot of it now, which there was not before.

events.text: Sixty years, or it might be eighty. There is a house on the dyke with a better roof, and a family in it with big hands and small opinions, who bring a cup down to your water at the new year. They no longer know why. One of them is called the same as {bk_child}, more or less. They say a line of a song to the pool on the way out, without thinking. It is the wrong words. You are so glad.

choices.text: Send them a good year's fish

effects.log: The nets come up heavy for one whole season. They put it down to the moon. You let them.

choices.text: Lie still, and let them not know

effects.log: You lie still. It is enough to know that there is someone on the dyke with a bad knee in the wet.

events.text: A stranger from three provinces away comes to the pool in a good coat. {bk_child}'s people have gone a long way since the dyke. They have a scholar now and a sword teacher. The stranger takes off a hat, and looks down at the water as though it owed something, and takes a very long breath, and goes in. It takes a good while. You hold quite still, and you are not at all surprised when they come up again.

choices.text: Show yourself once, far down, and let them see

effects.log: They look at you for as long as that breath lasts. They bow in the water, badly. It runs in the family.

choices.text: Stay out of sight. Let them think that the pool is only a pool

effects.log: They go away disappointed, and that is a safe thing to be. You have had quite enough of telling people what they are.

events.text: You had said never again. {npc} has lost a goat, and has been shouting for it up and down the bank in a very carrying voice, with a great deal of original language, on the wrong night of the wrong month. You find yourself up on the bank in the good robe, holding the goat. {He} takes it, and {he} looks at your wet hem, and asks if you are the one that the old people talk about. You are so tired of the deep.

choices.text: Say yes. Tell {him} all of it, before anything starts

effects.log: {He} hears you out, sitting on the goat. It takes until dawn. "And the rooster?" {he} says. "I have a dog," {he} says. It is not the same at all. It is not supposed to be.

choices.text: Hand over the goat, and go home

effects.log: You go home. You stand under the falls until the whole thing has washed off, and it takes rather longer than you meant it to.

events.text: A person comes to the pool with no fear at all, sits down on the rock that the heron uses, and takes off a hat. You have never seen them in this life, and the water knows them. They are a long way from any house of yours. They do not even look surprised. "I had it all from a very old story," they say to the water. "I only came to see if it was true. It is good to see you are doing well."

choices.text: Rise, and let them see all of you

effects.log: You look at one another for an hour or so. They bow, get up, and put on the hat. You were a story to them, and they to you, and it seems neither of you minds.

choices.text: Stay down, and send up one long breath

effects.log: The bubbles come up at the rock. They laugh out loud. On their way out of the valley they are humming something, and you cannot quite hear what it is.

events.text: You can hold your breath for longer than the other children can. You find this out at the mill pool when the older ones hold you under for a joke, and after a while they get frightened and let go, and you have been looking at some very interesting stones. {npc}, who has known this family longer than anyone will say, takes you home and rubs your hair dry and asks you to do that less.

choices.text: Ask why

effects.log: "You will want a hat," says {npc}, "by and by." And that is all that you get. It is a strange thing to say to a child, and you keep it for years.

choices.text: Promise. Do it anyway, but where nobody can see

effects.log: You find a deeper place. It is much better down there. Nobody ever asks you anything, and you always come up on time.

events.text: There is a thing that happens to your skin in spring. It starts behind the knees and goes dry and pale, and lifts away in one long piece if you are careful. {npc} comes on you behind the woodshed with a whole arm of it in your hand. {He} does not shout. {He} takes it from you, and looks at it in the light, and burns it in the stove, then shows you how to do it faster.

choices.text: Ask whether everyone does this

effects.log: "Everyone on our side of it," says {npc}, and goes on feeding the stove. {He} seems to think that this was an answer.

choices.text: Say nothing, and keep the next one

effects.log: You keep it in a box. It weighs nothing at all. You like to look at it when things have gone badly at school.

events.text: The persimmon, the well, the dyke: it does not matter where you are. When a rain is coming you know it a day ahead, in your teeth. This year you say so, out loud, in front of the headman, with the sky as clean as a plate. Everyone laughs. By nightfall they have stopped. {npc} looks at you over the heads of the others and just slightly shakes {his} head.

choices.text: Say it was a lucky guess

effects.log: They believe you, because it is easier. You spend the next few years being wrong about the weather on purpose, and you get rather good at that as well.

choices.text: Tell them about the next one too

effects.log: They begin to come to you before they cut the hay. It is very pleasant. Some of the older ones have also begun to leave a space around you on the road.

events.text: Your sixteenth summer, in the river, with the current stronger than you are. Then it is not. Something in your back unlocks, one bone after another, and you are sitting on a rock above the falls with your heart going very slowly when {npc} gets there, out of breath. {He} looks at the falls and at you. "Well," {he} says. "Sit, and I will tell you who it was that came to the back door."

choices.text: Hear all of it

effects.log: A robe, a thread, a child called {bk_line}. And the one in the pool, {bk_anc}. You have a long think. {npc} has brought food, and has clearly been meaning to have this talk for some time.

choices.text: Tell {him} that you do not want to know

effects.log: {npc} nods, and eats {his} rice. "It does not change the falls," {he} says. You go home by the road, on foot, and it takes all day.

events.text: There is a rumour in the district, and it has reached you. Someone's cousin has seen a person walk out of the river at the ford, dry to the knees, at a bad time of night. The rumour is that this person will need to be looked into. {npc} tells you this while slicing radish. {He} is very good with a knife. {He} also mentions that the family has moved four times in a hundred years, and is usually quite good at it.

choices.text: Stay, and start being seen at noon

effects.log: You make a point of going to market and buying things, loudly, and getting sunburnt. It is the best disguise there is. By winter the talk has moved on to the miller.

choices.text: Go down to the ford and see who is asking

effects.log: They are young and bored, and they have a very cheap net. You stand and chat with them for some time. You have rarely been so offended.

events.text: An old woman from the far end of the valley has come by to look at you. The old woman looks a good while, then turns your hand palm up and lays a needle in it, threaded with red. "Your people owe mine a needle," says the old woman. "It is very old. I said I would bring it, if I lived." No explanation is given. {npc} sees the old woman out, and they talk at the gate as if neither of them were young, or ever had been.

choices.text: Keep the needle, and ask {npc} what that was

effects.log: It takes {him} two bottles to tell you. Yours was not the only family with somebody on the back step. Some of them were not lucky. You keep the needle in your collar, from then on.

choices.text: Run it through the hem of your own coat

effects.log: You wear it so. You could not say why. It is cold in the wet, and it tugs a little when you walk toward water, and {npc} sees it there and goes quiet.

events.text: A flood year. The dyke goes in the night, and you are in the water before you have thought, with somebody's grandfather under one arm and a pig under the other. You come up in front of the whole village by torchlight. You have been down for a great deal longer than any person can. They look at you. Nobody says it. A child starts to, and is hushed. {npc} walks through with a blanket as if it were any evening.

choices.text: Go back in for the others

effects.log: You make eleven more trips. Nobody ever mentions it, and there is a good cut of meat at your door for years, and no one who will marry into the family.

choices.text: Cough, and shake, and let them carry you home

effects.log: You do it very well. You lie in bed for a week, being an ordinary person who nearly drowned. There are some who believe it. {npc} brings you broth and calls you an idiot, fondly.

events.text: It is {npc}'s birthday, or it is a quiet night, or you have run out of ways to say why you do not go near the water with the children. {He} is mending something by the lamp. You have been lying for years now, and {he} has been letting you. It occurs to you what the needle in your collar is really for. {He} looks up. You have the whole of the old story, there in your mouth.

choices.text: Tell {him} who it was that came to the back door

effects.log: {He} hears you out, and {he} goes on sewing for quite some time. "So that is why the well likes you," {he} says. And then: "I knew about the skin." You sit there, and you are as frightened as you have ever been, and very happy.

choices.text: Say that it is only a cold, and go to bed

effects.log: It goes on being only a cold, year after year. {He} leaves a dry shirt by the door on wet nights, and does not ask. You could not say which of you it is that this is for.

events.text: {npc} is holding {his} breath in the washtub. You come in to find {him} at it, small face down, the water quite still, and from the way {he} looks up at you this has been going on for a while, and {he} is pleased with it. You know how this goes from here. Someone will hold {him} under for a joke. You look at the water and at the hat on the peg.

choices.text: Teach {him}. Slowly, and all of it

effects.log: So you go down to the mill pool at dawn. {He} is better at it than you were. You tell {him} about the hat, the skin and the rooster, and {he} takes it all as a child takes anything, with interest, and then asks for food.

choices.text: Lift {him} out. Say it is a bad game

effects.log: You dry {his} hair, and say nothing else. {He} looks at you carefully. {He} will find some deeper place. You know that, because you did.

events.text: {npc} has come into the district with a very good letter and a very long hook. {He} is a hunter of things in pools, and {he} has been buying drinks. There are three sects who pay well for a serpent's gall, and a physician in the capital who pays better for the blood of anything that was born of one. {He} finds you at the ford. {He} is pleasant. {He} asks you how long you can hold your breath.

choices.text: Answer {him} with your hands

ok.log: {He} goes into the river, hook and all, and comes up a good way down, with an altered view of things. {He} will not be the last. But {he} will think hard about being the next.

fail.log: {He} is very much better than {he} looks. You are in the water with a hole in your side, breathing it, and for once you are glad to be what you are.

choices.text: Say that you get winded on the stairs

effects.log: You cough for {him}, and you say that you are not a swimmer. {He} smiles, and pays for the drinks, and makes a small note in a small book.

events.text: {npc} again, greyer, with the book. It has been a long hunt, and {he} has grown fond of you, in the manner of hunters. {He} sits down across the fire with no hook in sight. "I know all about the pool," {he} says. "I have found your {bk_anc}. I would never get near it. But you could walk me up to the water, and it would come to you. Name a price. Or I can wait until you have children."

choices.text: Finish this, here, tonight

ok.log: It is short, and very quiet, and you sink the book with {him}, in the deep part of the river. You sit for a long while afterwards with your hands in the water. Nobody will ask about it.

fail.log: {He} has been waiting for this for ten years, and {he} is ready. You get away down the river with your ribs broken. {He} still has the book, and you have nothing left to hide.

choices.text: Tell {him} you do not know what {he} is talking about

effects.log: {He} nods, and looks into the fire. "No," {he} says, "you would not." {He} leaves in the morning. You move the family that same spring. It is the fifth time in a hundred years, and everyone is very good at it.

events.text: You wake up standing in the pool with your good coat on. It has happened three times this year. The water is at your chin, and it is the dark of the moon, and you have walked two li in your sleep. Down below you something very large has turned over. It does not want anything. It has only noticed. {npc} is sitting on the bank, with a lamp and a blanket, and {he} has clearly been there for a while.

choices.text: Go on down

effects.log: You go as far as the breath will take you, and it takes you a long way. It is not a dream, or else it is one with a very cold floor. You come up at sunrise feeling more like yourself than you have ever felt, and that frightens {npc} badly.

choices.text: Walk out, and sleep with a rope on your ankle

effects.log: You tie it to the bedpost and give {npc} the knot. It holds. In the mornings your ankle has a mark on it, and you have been pulling at it, all night, in one direction.

events.text: There has been no rain for a hundred days, and the old people have started to look at you. Nobody says it. They bring you a chicken for no reason. The headman comes to talk about the roof, and the headman has clearly been told to. You have never tried it, you do not know how, and it is in your back teeth and all down your spine like a word that you have forgotten. {npc} says only: "It costs."

choices.text: Go up the hill, and try

effects.log: You stand there until your nose bleeds. Two days later, there is a small cold rain on one small village. They are so grateful. You have aged, a little, somewhere that does not show.

choices.text: Say you do not understand them. Send a chicken back

effects.log: The wells get low. They do not bring you any more chickens, and nobody blames you, out loud. There is a very dry autumn, and you know just how much of it was yours.

events.text: {npc} takes you up there at last, on a night with no moon. {He} is a very old person to be climbing, and {he} does not stop to rest. It is only a pool under a waterfall that has no name. You have dreamed of it all your life, and it is smaller. {npc} sits down on a rock, and waits, and after a while the whole surface lifts by one hand's breadth, with no sound at all. {bk_anc} knows you. It has been very patient.

choices.text: Walk in, up to the neck, and say your name

effects.log: It takes a long time for anything to happen. Something the size of a road comes by you in the dark, slowly, without touching. When you climb out, your hands have stopped shaking for the first time in your life.

choices.text: Bow from the bank, and stay dry

effects.log: You bow as you have seen it done. The water goes down again, by a hand's breadth, and it seems to you that this was the correct answer. {npc} is quite silent, on the way down.

events.text: Whatever is left of {bk_anc}, in your time, it has sent for you. You can feel it in your hem. You come up at the dark of the moon, and it is all there on the rock in the rain, laid out as if a child had done it: a very old sword from the river bed, a pearl, a bowl. There is also a stretch of red thread, gone black, that has been kept, somewhere, for a very long time. {npc} takes off {his} hat.

choices.text: Take the thread

effects.log: It comes apart in your fingers, nearly. You will keep it in the box with the old skin. You could not say what it means, except that somebody once had the choice, and let it run.

choices.text: Take the sword. You are going to need it

effects.log: It is very heavy, and very good. The hilt is the wrong size for any hand you have ever seen. {npc} looks at it, and at you, and asks you what you think that it was for.

events.text: The skin comes off more quickly now. {npc} sits with you at the water. "You cannot go on like this," {he} says, "half of you holding the other half under." It is true. You could go down there now and not come back up, a very long thing, and very patient. You could go to the old physician and have it burned out. There is one more way, and {he} has only heard of it being done.

choices.text: Have it burned out. You will die on dry land, under a roof

effects.log: It takes a whole summer, and you would not want to do it again. In the autumn you go out in the rain, and it is only rain.

choices.text: Go down, and stop holding your breath

effects.log: You leave your good coat folded on the rock. You come back sometimes, in the years after, to walk on the road; and people are very polite.

choices.text: Keep the door open. Go down, and come home for dinner

effects.log: It should not be possible. You do it for some time before anyone notices that it is hard. {npc} says only that you owe a good deal to someone who once let a thread run.

events.text: You catch a cold, the first of your life. You are delighted. You go about the village sneezing and telling people. It goes down into your chest, and {npc} brings you broth, and looks at you for a long time, as you might look at a house with the fire out. You sit with your feet in the mill pool in the summer, and it is cold, and wet, and nothing in it has any idea who you are.

choices.text: Learn to swim, badly, like anyone

effects.log: You thrash about like everybody else, and the children laugh at you. You have never been so bad at anything. It is wonderful, most days.

choices.text: Go up the hill once, and leave a cup, and not stop

effects.log: You leave it on the rock and go. You do not look at the water. There is no one in it that you know, now, and you say so aloud, in case that would help.

events.text: It is said that there is someone in the river who will carry a child to shore, and that you should not thank them. You come up on feast days, in the coat. It fits less well each time. {npc} still sets out a bowl on the step when you come. You have the thought that you are the night visitor now, on that road, with the same bad feet, and you are amused. It is not a human way to be amused.

choices.text: Keep the feast days, as long as the coat will go on

effects.log: You will. You do not eat much. They seat you near the door, with a good view of the water, and the children dare each other to look at your hands.

choices.text: Stop going. Let them have the story

effects.log: You stop. A cup still comes down to the water at the new year, and you take that. You have come to think that it is the better half of the bargain, for both sides.

events.text: You keep two sets of clothes and a very strict arrangement with a rooster. In the winter you are at the bottom of the pool with your heart going once an hour, and in the spring you turn up with a sack of river pearls and complaints about the price of salt. {npc} says it is the most ridiculous thing {he} has ever seen. {He} does not stop laughing for some time.

choices.text: Carry a message across, from the water to the house

effects.log: The dry years are less dry on that side of the valley, somehow, and the pool has fewer drowned in it. Nobody can quite say who it was they made a bargain with.

choices.text: Say nothing to either, and go on as you are

effects.log: You go on, with a hat and a hook-scar. You owe nobody an explanation. It is the one thing all your relatives had in common.

events.text: You are very old now, for a person, and you have started to tell the children the story wrong on purpose. In your version, the girl does not run the needle through. They object. They know how it goes. {npc}, who has come in with the tea and who is not nearly as old as the last one who used to do this, says that you always get the second verse wrong in any case. You are very pleased.

choices.text: Tell it the true way, this once

effects.log: You tell it right, with the thread, and the morning, and the pool. The little one asks if it hurt. You think about that for a good while. "It was a very long way to walk," you tell them.

choices.text: Tell it wrong again

effects.log: The girl says, "Oh, come in out of the rain, then." The children are disgusted. Nobody gets drowned, and everybody lives on the dyke. It is the best story you know.

events.text: You have them carry you down to the water, this last autumn. They are big-handed and practical and there are a good many of them, and they have stopped asking why. {npc} tucks the blanket in. The surface of the pool is quite still. You take off your hat, and hold it on your knees. Nobody has seen the top of your head for some time, and you hear someone behind you draw in a very small breath.

choices.text: Say nothing. Let them look

effects.log: You sit there with the wind on your scalp until the evening. Nobody says a word about it. They will be telling that one, with mistakes, for a very long time.

choices.text: Hum the song, wrong words and all

effects.log: One of them knows it. It turns out that they all do. The whole hill is at it by the second verse, flat, and far out in the pool something goes by, not hurrying.
